title: Genetic photosensitivity disorders
summary: Genetic photosensitivity disorders, established as described in 8.00E. A) Xeroderma pigmentosum — disabled from birth; OR B) Other genetic photosensitivity disorder with extensive skin lesions for 12+ months OR inability to function outside a highly protective environment for 12+ months.

children.criterion: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) — consider the individual disabled from birth

Other genetic photosensitivity disorder with (B.1) extensive skin lesions OR (B.2) inability to function outside a highly protective environment, in either case for a continuous period of at least 12 months
Genetic photosensitivity disorder other than XP (e.g., porphyria, erythropoietic protoporphyria, Cockayne syndrome, Bloom syndrome)
Any one of B.1 (extensive skin lesions) or B.2 (inability to function outside protective environment), each lasting at least 12 continuous months
Extensive skin lesions (see 8.00C1) that have lasted or can be expected to last for a continuous period of at least 12 months
Inability to function outside of a highly protective environment for a continuous period of at least 12 months (see 8.00E2)
